questions.stem: In this color-Doppler echocardiogram of a patent ductus arteriosus, what does the bright mosaic (multicolored) signal at the pulmonary-artery end most likely represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Normal antegrade flow across the pulmonary valve

choices.label: E
choices.text: A calcified thrombus occluding the duct

explanation.summary: The high pressure gradient from aorta to pulmonary artery accelerates flow through the duct; the resulting turbulence exceeds the Nyquist limit and appears as a mosaic of aliased colors on Doppler.
explanation.whyCorrect: The high pressure gradient from aorta to pulmonary artery accelerates flow through the duct; the resulting turbulence exceeds the Nyquist limit and appears as a mosaic of aliased colors on Doppler.

questions.stem: This photograph shows a patient with a PDA whose lower-extremity oxygen saturation (foot probe) is markedly lower than the upper-extremity saturation (hand probe). What mechanism best explains this pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A left-to-right shunt through an atrial septal defect

choices.label: B
choices.text: Right-to-left shunting into the aorta distal to the head/arm vessels

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aortic coarctation located proximal to the left subclavian artery

choices.label: E
choices.text: Methemoglobinemia selectively affecting the lower limbs

explanation.summary: In Eisenmenger physiology the reversed PDA shunt delivers deoxygenated blood to the descending aorta beyond the arch vessels, so the legs appear cyanotic (differential cyanosis) while the upper body remains pink.
explanation.whyCorrect: In Eisenmenger physiology the reversed PDA shunt delivers deoxygenated blood to the descending aorta beyond the arch vessels, so the legs appear cyanotic (differential cyanosis) while the upper body remains pink.

questions.stem: This schematic depicts an atrial septal defect. Why does blood cross the defect in the direction shown rather than the reverse?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Left atrial pressure normally exceeds right atrial pressure

choices.label: B
choices.text: The septal defect actively pumps blood toward the left

choices.label: C
choices.text: Right atrial pressure normally exceeds left atrial pressure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pulmonary artery pressure exceeds systemic arterial pressure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gravity directs blood across the interatrial septum

explanation.summary: Because the left atrium operates at higher pressure than the right, an interatrial communication produces a left-to-right shunt, increasing pulmonary blood flow.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because the left atrium operates at higher pressure than the right, an interatrial communication produces a left-to-right shunt, increasing pulmonary blood flow.

questions.stem: This diagram shows the normal sequence of fetal atrial septation. Failure of the septum primum to fuse with the endocardial cushions produces which type of defect?

explanation.summary: Persistence of the ostium primum from incomplete fusion of the septum primum with the endocardial cushions yields a primum ASD, located low in the atrial septum.
explanation.whyCorrect: Persistence of the ostium primum from incomplete fusion of the septum primum with the endocardial cushions yields a primum ASD, located low in the atrial septum.

questions.stem: This diagram illustrates formation of the interventricular septum. The membranous portion forms from fusion of the endocardial cushions, the aorticopulmonary septum, and which additional structure?

explanation.summary: The membranous IV septum completes when the muscular septum, the endocardial cushions, and the aorticopulmonary (conotruncal) septum meet; failure of this fusion is the most common cause of a VSD.
explanation.whyCorrect: The membranous IV septum completes when the muscular septum, the endocardial cushions, and the aorticopulmonary (conotruncal) septum meet; failure of this fusion is the most common cause of a VSD.

questions.stem: Comparing the normal heart with the heart with a VSD in this diagram, why is the oxygen saturation in the right ventricle higher than normal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coronary sinus blood draining into the right ventricle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Retrograde flow from aortic valve regurgitation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased oxygen extraction by the pulmonary circulation

explanation.summary: Oxygenated LV blood crosses the VSD into the RV, raising RV oxygen saturation (an oxygen 'step-up') detectable on catheterization.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oxygenated LV blood crosses the VSD into the RV, raising RV oxygen saturation (an oxygen 'step-up') detectable on catheterization.
